summary: Red Bluff sits at the northern end of the Sacramento Valley where the landscape transitions from flat agricultural bottomland to the volcanic foothills rolling toward Mount Lassen, and the Sacramento River cuts right through the center of town — one of the few small California cities where a major river is genuinely part of the daily scenery rather than hidden behind levees. That setting delivers 9.1 hours of sunshine per day on average and summer highs that routinely push well past the mid-70s annual average, making this unmistakably a hot-summer inland valley. A median home value of $271,100 against a median household income of around $50,200 produces a price-to-income ratio near 5.4 — more accessible than much of California, though a 17.6% poverty rate signals that the local economy, anchored by agriculture, government services, and the regional medical center, doesn't generate high wages broadly. The town's 7.7 square miles at roughly 1,900 people per square mile feel neither dense nor sprawling; a historic Main Street grid exists near the river, but connectivity frays quickly toward the I-5 corridor that bisects the area. Property crime runs notably high at about 5,841 per 100,000, with larceny alone accounting for the vast majority. Red Bluff is essentially a small county seat doing county-seat things — practical, sun-scorched, river-threaded — where affordability comes packaged with limited economic complexity.
